If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast bias toward overestimation in mid-horizon (days 10–20).  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast bias toward underestimation in early-horizon (days 1–10).  
When sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, accelerate upward correction in late-horizon (days 20–30) by 15–20% of residual error.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast consistently overestimates, apply downward bias of 5–10% to late-horizon (days 20–30) to align with true path.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast shows persistent downward drift, apply upward bias of 5–10% to mid-horizon (days 10–20) to counteract sentiment-driven momentum.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is flat or slightly upward, apply downward bias of 10–15% to early-horizon (days 1–10) to prevent overcorrection.
